answer: Spectral gap of the trust graph at the nectar threshold: each new identity adds one node but must attach via vouched edges to existing communities. The ledge is the second eigenvalue — farms pushing sybils inside a single cluster collapse it, exposing the cut. A mirror graph of reciprocal attestations doubles the edge cost per fake identity. Break-even: forging k colluding nodes costs O(k²) attestations while spectral detection flags clusters above 20% density, so returns die before k=15.
